title: Lipid nanoparticles for mRNA delivery
abstract: Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) are the most clinically advanced non-viral platform for mRNA delivery, exemplified by the COVID-19 vaccines. LNPs consist of four key components: ionizable lipids, helper phospholipids, cholesterol, and PEG-lipids. The ionizable lipid is the key determinant of potency, facilitating mRNA encapsulation and endosomal escape. Despite clinical success, LNPs have limitations: they primarily accumulate in the liver after intravenous administration, exhibit limited endosomal escape efficiency, and can induce inflammatory responses. Here, we review the design principles of LNPs, their structure-activity relationships, and emerging strategies for tissue-specific delivery. We identify several key gaps: the exact mechanism of endosomal escape remains controversial, extrahepatic targeting strategies have limited success in vivo, and the relationship between lipid pKa and in vivo efficacy is incompletely understood.

title: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles for RNA delivery: design, mechanism, and applications
abstract: Ionizable lipids are the central functional component of lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) for RNA delivery. These lipids are positively charged at low pH (enabling RNA encapsulation) and neutral at physiological pH (reducing toxicity). The field has progressed from early cationic lipids to modern ionizable lipids such as DLin-MC3-DMA, SM-102, and ALC-0315. Key structure-activity relationships include the influence of tail length, unsaturation, and headgroup pKa on delivery efficiency. The pKa of ionizable lipids correlates with in vivo potency, with an optimal pKa around 6.2-6.5 for hepatocyte delivery. However, mechanistic understanding of how ionizable lipids facilitate endosomal escape is still evolving. Current evidence suggests that ionizable lipids disrupt the endosomal membrane through a flip-flop mechanism involving protonation-deprotonation cycles, but direct experimental evidence for this model remains limited.

title: Combinatorial design of ionizable lipids for lipid nanoparticle delivery of mRNA
abstract: We report a combinatorial library of 120 ionizable lipids synthesized via Michael addition chemistry to identify novel lipid structures for mRNA delivery. The library varied alkyl tail length, amine headgroup chemistry, and linker composition. Top candidates were formulated into LNPs and screened for in vitro mRNA delivery in HeLa and Hep3B cells. The most potent lipids contained imidazole-based headgroups and C12-C14 alkyl tails. Lead formulations achieved mRNA expression levels comparable to MC3-based LNPs in mice after intravenous administration, with improved tolerability. Systematic analysis revealed that lipid pKa, tail volume, and unsaturation independently contribute to delivery efficiency. However, translation to extrahepatic tissues was not achieved, and the precise relationship between lipid structure and intracellular trafficking remains poorly understood.

title: Endosomal escape of lipid nanoparticles: a mechanistic investigation
abstract: The mechanism by which lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) escape the endosome is not fully understood. Using a combination of fluorescence microscopy, cryo-electron tomography, and lipid mixing assays, we investigated the intracellular trafficking of LNPs in HeLa and DC2.4 cells. We observed rapid internalization via clathrin-mediated endocytosis, followed by accumulation in early endosomes. Using a newly developed content release assay, we quantified LNP-mediated release of fluorescently labeled mRNA into the cytosol. We found that less than 5% of internalized mRNA reached the cytosol, indicating that endosomal escape is a major bottleneck. Ionizable lipids promoted membrane destabilization through a pH-dependent phase transition from lamellar to inverted hexagonal structures. Helper lipids, particularly DOPE, enhanced this effect. These findings suggest that endosomal escape efficiency must be improved at least 10-fold for LNP-based therapeutics to achieve their full potential.

title: Extrahepatic targeting of lipid nanoparticles in vivo
abstract: Clinical use of lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) is limited by their predominant accumulation in the liver after systemic administration. We explored two strategies for extrahepatic targeting: ligand conjugation and tuning of lipid composition. Conjugation of anti-CD3 antibodies to LNP surfaces achieved T-cell-specific mRNA delivery with 60% transfection efficiency in vitro but only 15% in vivo due to opsonization and clearance. Incorporation of PEG-lipids with shorter PEG chains reduced liver uptake from 85% to 60% and increased protein expression in spleen and lungs. However, no formulation achieved significant targeting to muscle, heart, or brain. A major barrier is the rapid formation of a protein corona on LNPs after injection, which masks targeting ligands and redirects particles to the liver. These findings underscore the need for fundamental advances in understanding nano-bio interactions to achieve extrahepatic targeting.

title: CRISPR-Cas9 lipid nanoparticle systems for in vivo gene editing
abstract: Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) have emerged as promising carriers for CRISPR-Cas9 components for in vivo gene editing. We developed an LNP formulation co-encapsulating Cas9 mRNA and sgRNA targeting the PCSK9 gene. After a single intravenous injection in mice, we observed 80% reduction in serum PCSK9 levels that persisted for over 100 days. However, editing efficiency varied widely across tissues: 60-70% in liver, 15-20% in spleen, and undetectable in lung, kidney, and muscle. High-performance LNPs with optimized ionizable lipid MC3 achieved the highest editing in hepatocytes, but extrahepatic editing remains elusive. Attempts to increase extrahepatic delivery by modifying the lipid composition resulted in reduced overall potency. The immunogenicity of LNP-delivered Cas9 also remains a concern, with anti-Cas9 antibodies detected after repeat administration. These results highlight the need for novel LNP designs that can access diverse cell types while avoiding immune recognition.

title: Structure-activity relationships of ionizable lipids for lipid nanoparticle delivery
abstract: We synthesized and evaluated 100+ ionizable lipidoids to understand structure-activity relationships (SAR) for mRNA delivery. Key findings: (1) lipid pKa between 6.0-6.8 is critical for in vivo potency, (2) unsaturated tails (C18:1, C18:2) outperform saturated tails, (3) ester linkages improve biodegradability without sacrificing activity, (4) tail length of C12-C16 provides optimal delivery. Using machine learning, we identified that tail volume and headgroup hydrogen bonding capacity are the most predictive features for delivery efficiency. However, the same SAR rules do not apply across different administration routes (IV vs IM vs SC). Intramuscular delivery tolerates a wider pKa range than IV delivery. Important gaps remain: the role of lipid shape in membrane curvature induction during endosomal escape is poorly characterized, and most SAR studies have been limited to a small number of cell types.

title: Biodistribution and pharmacokinetics of lipid nanoparticle-formulated mRNA
abstract: Understanding the pharmacokinetics and biodistribution of LNP-mRNA is critical for therapeutic development. We administered luciferase-encoding mRNA formulated in MC3-based LNPs to mice and quantified mRNA distribution and protein expression over time. Peak expression occurred at 6 hours post-injection and declined to baseline by day 7. The liver accounted for 82% of total luciferase signal, followed by spleen (12%), and lungs (3%). Tissue homogenate analysis showed that 92% of the injected dose accumulated in the liver within 30 minutes. Surprisingly, despite rapid hepatic uptake, only 2-5% of internalized mRNA was translated into protein, suggesting that LNP unpackaging and endosomal escape within hepatocytes is inefficient. Repeated administration at 4-week intervals showed no reduction in expression over 4 doses. However, anti-PEG IgM antibodies were detected after the first dose, potentially accelerating clearance of subsequent doses. These data highlight the need for improved endosomal escape and strategies to avoid the accelerated blood clearance phenomenon.

title: Small interfering RNA delivery via lipid nanoparticles for liver target engagement
abstract: Patisiran (Onpattro), an LNP-formulated siRNA targeting transthyretin (TTR), was the first FDA-approved RNAi therapeutic. Clinical outcomes demonstrate that LNPs can achieve robust, dose-dependent target engagement in hepatocytes, with 80-90% TTR knockdown sustained over months. The approved formulation uses DLin-MC3-DMA as the ionizable lipid. Despite this success, several challenges remain: (1) extrahepatic delivery has not been clinically achieved, (2) LNP-mediated siRNA delivery requires relatively high doses (0.3 mg/kg), (3) the mechanism of intracellular release remains incompletely understood, and (4) immunogenicity limits repeat dosing. Comparison of MC3-DMA with newer ionizable lipids (e.g., SM-102, L319) shows that modifications improving endosomal escape often increase inflammatory responses. This tradeoff between potency and tolerability represents a fundamental challenge in LNP design.

title: mRNA vaccines against COVID-19: a perspective on LNP formulation design
abstract: The two mRNA vaccines authorized for COVID-19 (BNT162b2 by BioNTech/Pfizer and mRNA-1273 by Moderna) use LNP technology to deliver nucleoside-modified mRNA encoding the spike protein. Both LNPs contain ionizable lipids that are structurally distinct: SM-102 in mRNA-1273 and ALC-0315 in BNT162b2. Comparative analysis reveals that the LNP composition significantly impacts vaccine potency, thermostability, and reactogenicity. The BNT162b2 formulation requires storage at -80°C, while mRNA-1273 is stable at -20°C. Both vaccines achieve >90% efficacy, but the durability of protection wanes over 6-8 months. Immune responses are characterized by robust neutralizing antibody titers and T-cell responses. Key gaps include: (1) mechanisms of LNP-induced inflammation remain poorly understood, (2) the contribution of specific lipid components to immune activation versus delivery efficiency is unclear, and (3) developing thermostable formulations that eliminate cold chain requirements remains a significant engineering challenge.

title: Nucleoside-modified mRNA-LNP therapeutics beyond vaccines: protein replacement and gene editing
abstract: While mRNA-LNP vaccines have been transformative for infectious disease, the platform holds promise for broader therapeutic applications including protein replacement therapy, cancer immunotherapy, and gene editing. In proof-of-concept studies, we delivered mRNA encoding human factor IX to mice with hemophilia B and achieved therapeutic levels of clotting activity for 7-10 days. Repeat dosing extended efficacy but with diminishing returns. For gene editing, co-delivery of Cas9 mRNA and sgRNA targeting a disease-associated gene achieved 15-30% editing in liver cells. Translation to non-hepatic tissues is limited by LNP tropism. Additionally, the requirement for repeat administration raises concerns about immunogenicity. Current LNPs are also less efficient at transducing primary cells compared to established cell lines, and the relationship between LNP composition and protein corona formation in different disease states is not understood.

title: Advances in lipid nanoparticle delivery of nucleic acids and beyond
abstract: Lipid nanoparticles have revolutionized nucleic acid delivery, enabling the clinical translation of mRNA vaccines and RNAi therapeutics. This review covers the evolution of LNP technology from early cationic liposomes to current state-of-the-art ionizable lipid nanoparticles. We discuss LNP formulation parameters including ionizable lipid structure, lipid ratios, particle size, and surface charge. We examine current understanding of LNP-cell interactions: cellular uptake (clathrin- and caveolae-mediated endocytosis), endosomal trafficking, and the poorly characterized mechanism of endosomal escape. New developments include: (1) microfluidic mixing methods enabling reproducible LNP production, (2) high-throughput screening platforms for novel lipid discovery, (3) incorporation of targeting ligands, and (4) combination with other therapeutic modalities. Major unresolved challenges include achieving efficient delivery to non-hepatic tissues, overcoming biological barriers such as the mucus and blood-brain barriers, and reducing immunogenicity.

title: Rapidly adaptable nanoparticle platforms for mRNA delivery to the lung
abstract: We developed a combinatorial library of lipid-like materials (lipidoids) for mRNA delivery to the lung via aerosolization. From a library of 240 lipidoids, we identified structures that enabled efficient mRNA expression in airway epithelial cells following intratracheal administration. The lead formulation achieved luciferase expression levels 100-fold higher than previous reports and enabled therapeutic levels of secreted protein in a mouse model of surfactant deficiency. However, delivery efficiency decreased by 80% when scaling from mice to rabbits, and repeat administration resulted in diminished returns due to innate immune activation. A key limitation is the lack of understanding of the biophysical interactions between LNPs and the mucus barrier. Furthermore, the relationship between lipidoid structure and tolerability in pulmonary tissues remains poorly characterized. These findings highlight the challenges of translating LNP technology across administration routes.

title: Lipid nanoparticle chemistry: from RNA delivery to the next generation of therapeutics
abstract: Lipid nanoparticle (LNP) technology has evolved from early cationic lipid formulations to sophisticated ionizable lipid systems optimized through rational design and combinatorial chemistry. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the chemical design space for ionizable lipids, including amine headgroups (tertiary amines, imidazoles, piperazines), linker chemistry (ester, amide, carbamate), and hydrophobic tails (unsaturated, branched, degradable). We discuss how lipid chemical structure influences nanoparticle properties including pKa, fluidity, fusogenicity, and biodegradability. Despite extensive SAR studies, fundamental questions remain: the precise molecular requirements for efficient endosomal escape are unknown, the role of lipid metabolism in nanoparticle clearance is underexplored, and predictive models for immunogenicity based on lipid structure have not been developed. Future directions include multi-component systems that combine delivery with sensing or therapeutic activity.

title: The endosomal escape of lipid nanoparticles: mechanisms and strategies for improvement
abstract: Endosomal escape is the most critical bottleneck for lipid nanoparticle (LNP)-mediated nucleic acid delivery. After cellular uptake via endocytosis, LNPs must rapidly escape the endosome to deliver their cargo to the cytosol before degradation. The prevailing model posits that the ionizable lipid becomes protonated in the acidic endosomal environment, promoting electrostatic interactions with anionic endosomal lipids and inducing non-bilayer structures that disrupt the membrane. However, direct visualization of this process in living cells has been challenging. Using a combination of advanced microscopy techniques and compartment-specific markers, we provide evidence that LNP-mediated endosomal escape involves both membrane destabilization and fusion events. We observed that less than 2% of LNP-encapsulated cargo reaches the cytosol, suggesting endosomal entrapment is the dominant barrier. Strategies to improve escape include tuning lipid pKa, incorporating fusogenic helper lipids, and using pH-responsive polymers. However, improvements in endosomal escape often correlate with increased toxicity, suggesting that potent escape and biocompatibility may require decoupling through novel chemical approaches.

title: Designing lipid nanoparticles for targeted delivery of nucleic acids to the brain
abstract: The blood-brain barrier (BBB) prevents most LNP-formulated nucleic acids from reaching the brain parenchyma. We explored several strategies to overcome this barrier: (1) conjugation of transferrin and glucose ligands to LNP surfaces, (2) formulation with BBB-penetrating peptides, and (3) direct intrathecal administration. Transferrin-targeted LNPs showed 3-fold higher brain accumulation in mice compared to non-targeted LNPs, but absolute brain levels remained below therapeutic thresholds. Intrathecal administration achieved broader CNS distribution but with significant inter-subject variability. A major limitation is that the optimal LNP composition for systemic administration differs from that for direct CNS administration, and the interplay between LNP surface chemistry and BBB transport mechanisms is poorly understood. These results indicate that brain delivery of LNP-nucleic acids remains a fundamental unsolved problem.

title: Immunogenicity of lipid nanoparticle-formulated mRNA: mechanisms and mitigation strategies
abstract: While LNP-formulated mRNA vaccines have been remarkably successful, the immunogenicity of LNP components themselves is increasingly recognized as a complex factor affecting both potency and safety. LNPs activate innate immune pathways through multiple mechanisms: (1) ionizable lipids trigger TLR4 signaling, (2) the PEG-lipid component can induce anti-PEG IgM antibodies, (3) mRNA itself (even with nucleoside modifications) stimulates endosomal TLR3/7/8 receptors at high doses, and (4) the nanoparticle structure acts as a damage-associated molecular pattern (DAMP). The balance between adjuvant effect (beneficial for vaccines) and inflammatory toxicity (harmful for therapeutic applications) is not well understood. We found that LNP-induced inflammation is composition-dependent: LNPs containing MC3 induced higher levels of IL-6 and TNF-alpha compared to SM-102-containing LNPs. Efforts to develop 'stealth' LNPs that avoid immune detection have had limited success, as reduced immunogenicity often correlates with reduced delivery efficiency. Decoupling immunogenicity from delivery remains a major challenge.

title: Microfluidic production of lipid nanoparticles for nucleic acid delivery
abstract: The clinical translation of LNP-nucleic acid therapeutics has been enabled by scalable microfluidic manufacturing processes. Using a microfluidic mixing device, LNPs are formed by rapid mixing of an ethanol phase containing lipids with an aqueous phase containing nucleic acids. Critical parameters include total flow rate, flow rate ratio, mixing time, and lipid composition. We systematically characterized how microfluidic mixing conditions affect LNP size, polydispersity, encapsulation efficiency, and in vivo potency. We found that mixing time <5 ms is necessary for optimal particle homogeneity. LNPs produced at higher total flow rates exhibited smaller size (40-60 nm vs 80-100 nm), higher encapsulation efficiency (>95%), and 2-fold higher in vivo expression. However, microfluidic manufacturing has not been validated for the wide range of lipid compositions being explored in preclinical studies, particularly for compositions incorporating targeting ligands or novel helper lipids. Scaling production to clinical batch sizes while maintaining product quality remains a significant engineering challenge.

title: SORT LNPs enable multi-organ mRNA delivery via selective organ targeting lipids
abstract: We introduce selective organ targeting (SORT) lipids that, when spiked into standard four-component LNPs, redirect mRNA delivery from liver to lung, spleen, or other tissues in a dose-dependent manner. Addition of permanently cationic SORT lipids increased lung protein expression more than 40-fold versus base LNPs, while anionic SORT lipids favored spleen delivery. We propose that SORT lipids remodel the protein corona and alter apolipoprotein binding, thereby changing tissue tropism. However, the molecular mechanism linking SORT lipid charge to corona composition remains poorly understood. Endosomal escape efficiency was not substantially improved, and less than 3% of delivered mRNA reached the cytosol in non-hepatic cells. These results show that organ targeting and intracellular delivery are separable bottlenecks.

title: Hybrid nucleic acid nanostructures for programmable intracellular delivery
abstract: DNA/RNA hybrid nanostructures offer sequence-programmable scaffolds for co-delivering mRNA and regulatory oligos. We hypothesized that bifunctional designs displaying both endosomal-disrupting peptides and tissue-targeting aptamers would outperform LNPs in extrahepatic models. In vitro, hybrid particles achieved 2.5-fold higher cytosolic delivery than matched LNPs, yet in vivo liver accumulation remained dominant after IV dosing. A major limitation is nuclease stability during circulation. We identify an untested claim in the field: that structured RNA can autonomously escape endosomes without ionizable lipids. Our data do not support this claim under physiological salt and serum conditions.

title: Quantitative single-cell map of LNP uptake, endosomal progression, and mRNA translation
abstract: Using barcoded mRNA and time-resolved single-cell RNA readout, we built a quantitative cascade map of LNP delivery in primary hepatocytes and T cells. Uptake varied only 3-fold across formulations, whereas endosomal escape varied more than 30-fold and explained most of the variance in protein output. We propose that helper-lipid packing parameter is the dominant determinant of escape once particles reach maturing endosomes. Results show that improving uptake alone yields diminishing returns. However, the exact molecular mechanism of bilayer disruption remains controversial, and direct cryo-ET evidence in primary immune cells is still limited.

title: Machine-guided design of degradable ionizable lipids for redosable mRNA LNPs
abstract: Chronic mRNA dosing is limited by lipid accumulation and innate activation. We used a graph neural network trained on 612 ionizable lipids to propose degradable ester-branched candidates. Lead lipid DL-17 matched SM-102 potency in mice at 0.1 mg/kg while reducing liver lipid residues by 70% at 48 h. Anti-PEG IgM titers after three weekly doses were reduced 2-fold versus SM-102 LNPs. We hypothesized that faster lipid clearance decouples potency from reactogenicity. Nevertheless, extrahepatic delivery was not achieved, and endosomal escape remained below 4% of internalized dose.

title: Lung-selective polymeric nanoparticles for inhaled mRNA: barriers beyond formulation
abstract: Inhaled mRNA therapies must cross mucus, avoid macrophages, and reach epithelial cytosol. We compare LNPs and biodegradable polymeric nanoparticles after aerosol dosing in mice and human airway cultures. Polymeric particles showed 5-fold higher epithelial association but only 1.2-fold higher protein expression, indicating a post-uptake bottleneck. Mucus binding reduced recoverable dose by 40%. We propose that mucin-nanoparticle affinity, not aerosol aerodynamics, is the primary barrier in diseased airways. The relationship between surface zwitterion density and mucus penetration remains poorly understood and is a key gap for clinical translation.

title: Zwitterionic ionizable lipids reduce complement activation while preserving hepatic mRNA expression
abstract: We report a 2024 series of zwitterionic ionizable lipids (ZILs) that incorporate a phosphorylcholine motif proximal to the ionizable amine. In human serum, ZIL LNPs cut C3a generation by 55% relative to SM-102 controls while retaining 90% of hepatic luciferase expression at 0.05 mg/kg in mice. Cryo-EM showed tighter bilayer packing and reduced protein corona diversity. We hypothesize that zwitterionic surface potential limits IgM docking without blocking ApoE-LDLR uptake. However, spleen and lung expression remained below 5% of liver signal. Endosomal escape efficiency improved only modestly (from 1.8% to 2.4% cytosolic cargo). These findings separate complement quieting from extrahepatic tropism as distinct design goals.

title: In situ PROTAC mRNA LNPs for controllable degradation of hepatic disease targets
abstract: Messenger RNA encoding a cereblon-based PROTAC was formulated in liver-tropic LNPs to degrade a model transmembrane protein in vivo. A single 0.2 mg/kg dose produced 80% target loss at 24 h with recovery by day 10. We propose that transient PROTAC expression avoids prolonged E3 ligase engagement toxicity seen with small-molecule dosing. Results show dose-linear knockdown between 0.05 and 0.3 mg/kg. A key limitation is that extrahepatic disease targets were not engaged due to LNP biodistribution. The safety of repeated PROTAC-mRNA cycles remains poorly understood, and immunogenicity of the degrader protein itself was not fully characterized.

title: Base-edited HSC mobilization via mRNA-LNP delivery of engraftment enhancers
abstract: We demonstrate transient mRNA-LNP delivery of CXCR4 modulators to mobilized hematopoietic stem cells, enabling higher peripheral yields without integrating viral vectors. In nonhuman primates, two doses increased CD34+ yield 3.1-fold. We hypothesized that short-lived protein expression would minimize off-target niche disruption. Experimental results confirmed niche markers normalized within 72 h. Nevertheless, endosomal escape in resting HSCs was inefficient, with less than 2% of cargo reaching cytosol. The exact mechanism of HSC-specific uptake after IV LNP dosing remains unclear, and scaling lipid supply for clinical apheresis workflows is an unresolved engineering barrier.

title: Spatially barcoded lipid nanoparticles reveal neighborhood-dependent tropism in solid tumors
abstract: A library of 96 chemically barcoded LNPs was administered to mice bearing orthotopic pancreatic tumors and decoded by spatial transcriptomics. Contrary to bulk biodistribution dogma, several low-liver formulations enriched in fibroblast-rich tumor neighborhoods rather than epithelial cores. We propose that local extracellular matrix charge and macrophage density jointly gate nanoparticle entry. Delivery efficiency dropped 8-fold from tumor margin to core. Extrahepatic targeting success in bulk assays therefore overstates functional delivery to malignant cells. The relationship between ionizable lipid pKa and matrix penetration is incompletely understood and warrants systematic study.

title: Circular RNA LNPs with orthogonal ionizable lipids for durable extrahepatic expression
abstract: Circular RNA (circRNA) payloads formulated with a newly designed orthogonal ionizable lipid OL-09 produced measurable protein in murine skeletal muscle after IM dosing for 28 days, versus 6 days for linear m1Ψ mRNA controls. IV dosing still favored liver, but muscle-to-liver expression ratio improved 4-fold versus SM-102. We hypothesized that slower circRNA turnover synergizes with lipids that reduce innate activation in myocytes. Cytokine panels showed 50% lower IL-6 peaks. However, endosomal escape in myofibers remains a major bottleneck, and less than 1.5% of internalized circRNA reached the cytosol. Fundamental advances in muscle endosomal trafficking assays are needed before dose predictions are reliable.

title: Bifunctional ncRNA-mRNA co-delivery reveals interference between RISC loading and translation
abstract: Hybrid LNPs co-encapsulating therapeutic mRNA and a bifunctional ncRNA designed to scaffold ribosomes while guiding RISC were tested in hepatocytes. We proposed that physical co-delivery would synchronize knockdown and replacement. Instead, high ncRNA fractions reduced mRNA translation by 60% without proportional increases in silencing, suggesting competition for endosomal escape capacity. Results show an optimal mass ratio near 1:8 ncRNA:mRNA. The mechanism of payload competition inside maturing endosomes remains poorly understood. This work identifies a previously under-tested tradeoff for bifunctional nucleic acid therapies sharing a single nanoparticle.

title: Serum-stable DNA-ionizable lipid hybrid nanoparticles for gene editing outside the liver
abstract: Replacing 30% of helper phospholipid with long single-stranded DNA scaffolds increased LNP stability in 50% human serum and raised spleen editing rates 2.2-fold for Cas9 mRNA plus sgRNA cargoes. We hypothesize that DNA scaffolds organize ionizable lipids into domains that resist premature PEG shedding. In vivo, liver editing still exceeded spleen editing by 5-fold, indicating incomplete redirection. Off-target indel analysis found no elevated genomic injury. A critical gap is the lack of mechanistic imaging showing whether DNA scaffolds alter endosomal membrane contact geometry. Scale-up of scaffold synthesis remains a practical barrier to clinical manufacturing.

title: Bifunctional guide–scaffold RNAs couple Cas9 editing to local transcript silencing
abstract: We designed bifunctional ncRNAs that simultaneously guide Cas9 to a genomic locus and scaffold AGO2 for local mRNA silencing. We hypothesized that physical coupling would reduce off-target transcript residual after editing. In HEK293 and primary T cells, dual-function guides achieved 45% on-target indels and 55% knockdown of residual alleles versus 48% indels and 20% knockdown with separate sgRNA plus siRNA. However, the mechanism of RISC loading from a Cas9-bound scaffold remains poorly understood. Endosomal delivery of these hybrid RNAs via LNPs was inefficient, with less than 3% cytosolic arrival. Results show payload competition when Cas9 mRNA is co-formulated. These findings identify an untested claim that bifunctional ncRNA can replace two-drug regimens without delivery redesign.

title: Aptamer-ncRNA chimeras for receptor-mediated cytosolic delivery without ionizable lipids
abstract: We propose that high-affinity transferrin receptor aptamers fused to structured ncRNA can mediate cytosolic delivery independent of ionizable lipids. In transferrin-receptor-high cells, aptamer-ncRNA chimeras increased uptake 6-fold versus untargeted RNA. Cytosolic reporter activity rose only 1.4-fold, indicating a post-uptake bottleneck. We hypothesized autonomous endosomal escape via RNA secondary structure; experimental results do not support this under serum conditions. A major limitation is nuclease cleavage of the aptamer stem within 30 minutes in human serum. The relationship between aptamer folding and endosomal membrane contact geometry remains poorly understood.

title: Circular RNA sponges as programmable sinks for microRNA networks in fibrotic lung
abstract: We engineered circRNA sponges with multivalent miR-21 and miR-29 binding sites for inhaled delivery. We hypothesized that multivalency would outcompete endogenous targets without AGO saturation toxicity. In bleomycin mice, polymeric nanoparticles delivering circ-sponge reduced collagen transcripts 40% at day 14. However, AGO occupancy assays showed partial saturation at high dose. Endosomal escape of circRNA in airway epithelium remained below 2% of internalized dose. Results show mucus binding reduced recoverable dose by 35%. The mechanism linking sponge topology to miRNA decay versus sequestration is controversial and warrants quantitative single-cell assays.

title: tRNA-like structural motifs stabilize linear mRNA without nucleoside modification
abstract: Appending viral tRNA-like structures (TLS) to linear mRNA 3' ends extended translation half-life 1.8-fold in hepatocytes without m1Ψ modification. We propose that TLS recruits host aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases that shield mRNA from exonuclease attack. Experimental results confirmed reduced 3' decay intermediates. Innate immune activation was higher than m1Ψ mRNA, with IL-6 elevated 2.2-fold. LNP delivery of TLS-mRNA matched SM-102 controls for peak expression but not durability in extrahepatic muscle. A key gap is whether TLS folding survives LNP encapsulation shear. The exact mechanism of synthetase-mediated shielding remains poorly understood.

title: Ribozyme–siRNA hybrids enable autocatalytic knockdown after endosomal escape
abstract: We designed hybrid oligonucleotides combining a hammerhead ribozyme and an siRNA guide to amplify silencing after a single escape event. In vitro, hybrids achieved 70% knockdown at 5-fold lower cytosolic concentration than siRNA alone. We hypothesized that ribozyme cleavage regenerates active guides inside the cytosol. Results support regeneration in buffer but not efficiently in crowded cytosol mimics. LNP co-delivery with ionizable lipids improved cytosolic arrival but reduced ribozyme activity 40%, suggesting lipid interactions denature catalytic folds. The tradeoff between catalytic fold integrity and LNP encapsulation is a fundamental unsolved problem.

title: Long noncoding RNA scaffolds organize chromatin editors delivered as mRNA-LNP
abstract: Transient mRNA-LNP delivery of epigenetic editors guided by synthetic lncRNA scaffolds was tested for locus-specific silencing of PCSK9. We proposed that lncRNA spatial organization would improve editor residence time without genomic integration. Liver editing of histone marks reached 60% at 48 h with recovery by day 21. Off-target chromatin peaks were detected at 12 loci. Endosomal escape limited dose efficiency, with less than 2.5% of lncRNA scaffold in cytosol. A major barrier is manufacturing long structured RNA at clinical purity. These results show hybrid ncRNA–editor systems are feasible but mechanism of scaffold-editor handoff remains unclear.

title: Chemical mapping of ionizable lipid–RNA phosphate contacts in bifunctional cargo LNPs
abstract: Using diazirine lipid probes and RNA-protein-lipid crosslinking, we mapped contact sites between ionizable lipids and bifunctional ncRNA–mRNA cargoes inside LNPs. We hypothesized that ncRNA GC-rich stems sequester ionizable amines and reduce mRNA protonation-driven escape. Crosslink density on ncRNA stems was 3.1-fold higher than on mRNA coding regions. Endosomal escape of mRNA dropped 50% when ncRNA fraction exceeded 20% by mass. Results show lipid–RNA contact geometry predicts payload competition better than bulk pKa. However, direct visualization in maturing endosomes is still limited, and the exact molecular mechanism of bilayer disruption remains controversial.

title: Spleen-selective SORT hybrids deliver antisense oligos against lncRNA MALAT1
abstract: Anionic SORT lipids redirected antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) LNPs toward spleen and reduced MALAT1 by 65% in marginal-zone B cells. We propose that corona remodeling, not ASO chemistry, dominates organ tropism. Experimental results confirmed ApoE reduction and complement factor enrichment on SORT particles. Endosomal escape in B cells remained inefficient (<2% cytosolic ASO). Extrahepatic targeting success in bulk assays overstated functional delivery to malignant B-cell subsets in a lymphoma model. The relationship between SORT charge and lncRNA-targeted ASO activity is incompletely understood.

title: Programmable RNA origami vehicles for co-delivery of Cas13 and guide arrays
abstract: RNA origami nanostructures packaged Cas13a protein and multiplex guides without ionizable lipids in vitro. We hypothesized that origami geometry would protect cargo and promote endosomal rupture via multivalent membrane engagement. In serum-free media, knockdown reached 80%. In 10% serum, activity collapsed to 15% due to nuclease attack and corona-induced aggregation. PEGylated origami improved circulation but blocked membrane engagement. These findings underscore that structured RNA vehicles still require hybrid lipid components for in vivo use. A key gap is predictive models for origami–endosome curvature matching.

title: MicroRNA–mRNA bifunctional LNPs reprogram macrophage phenotypes in solid tumors
abstract: LNPs co-encapsulating mRNA encoding IL-12 and a miR-155 mimic were tested in orthotopic pancreatic tumors. We proposed that bifunctional cargo would synchronize innate activation and cytokine production. Instead, high miRNA fractions reduced IL-12 translation 55% without proportional phenotype shifts, suggesting endosomal escape competition. Spatial barcoding showed delivery enriched at tumor margins. Results identify payload ratio as a critical design variable for macrophage reprogramming. The mechanism of miRNA versus mRNA escape kinetics remains poorly understood and is a high-priority experimental gap.

title: Pseudouridine synthase mRNA combined with substrate-selective gRNA scaffolds
abstract: We delivered mRNA encoding a programmable pseudouridine synthase together with guide ncRNA scaffolds targeting disease-associated transcripts. We hypothesized site-specific Ψ installation would stabilize transcripts without global epitranscriptomic disruption. On-target Ψ fraction reached 70% in hepatocytes at 0.3 mg/kg. Off-target Ψ increased 8% transcriptome-wide at high guide doses. LNP immunogenicity limited weekly redosing. A fundamental gap is the lack of single-molecule evidence that guide scaffolds remain bound during catalysis in living cells.

title: Dual-function ADAR recruiting RNAs for therapeutic A-to-I editing with reduced bystander edits
abstract: ADAR-recruiting guide RNAs (arRNAs) were optimized with structural modules that gate editing until target engagement. We propose that kinetic gating reduces bystander A-to-I edits. In mice, LNP-arRNA editing of a disease SNP reached 35% with 3-fold fewer bystanders than prior designs. However, delivery to extrahepatic tissues was minimal. Endosomal escape efficiency was not improved relative to mRNA LNPs. The exact structural mechanism of gating remains incompletely understood, and long-term ADAR perturbation safety is unknown.

title: Hybrid peptide–PNA oligomers for allele-selective silencing across the blood–brain barrier
abstract: Peptide nucleic acid (PNA) oligomers conjugated to BBB-shuttle peptides silenced a mutant allele in a Huntington mouse model after IV dosing. Brain levels remained below 0.2% ID/g. We hypothesized multivalent shuttles would raise parenchymal delivery; uptake rose 2-fold but functional silencing was unchanged, indicating a post-uptake barrier. Endosomal entrapment of PNA is a major bottleneck. Results show that hybrid peptide–nucleic acid chemistry alone does not solve cytosolic delivery in neurons. Mechanistic imaging of PNA escape in primary neurons is still limited.

title: Self-amplifying RNA with embedded miRNA target cassettes for cell-type restrictive expression
abstract: We embedded tandem miRNA target sites into self-amplifying RNA (saRNA) to suppress expression in off-target hepatocytes while allowing muscle expression after IM LNP dosing. Restrictive cassettes cut liver luciferase 70% with only 15% loss in muscle. We propose that miRNA gate efficiency depends on RISC availability after LNP inflammation. Experimental cytokine panels showed IL-6 peaks correlated with gate failure at high dose. Endosomal escape still limited absolute expression. The interplay between innate activation and miRNA gating is poorly characterized and represents a theory–experiment gap for safe saRNA vaccines.

title: Quantitative RNP profiling reveals ribosomal protein competition with LNP-delivered mRNA
abstract: After LNP mRNA delivery, we profiled ribonucleoprotein complexes and found ribosomal protein uS3 and helicases competing with initiation factors on exogenous mRNA. We hypothesized that ncRNA co-delivery could decoy these competitors. Decoy ncRNA improved translation 1.6-fold in hepatocytes but reduced overall escape efficiency, again showing payload competition. Results indicate cytosolic RNP competition is a post-escape bottleneck distinct from endosomal escape. The field has under-tested this mechanism relative to lipid chemistry optimization.

title: Glycan-masked LNPs for reduced anti-PEG responses during chronic siRNA dosing
abstract: Surface glycan masking of PEG-lipids reduced anti-PEG IgM titers 3-fold over five biweekly siRNA doses while preserving 85% of first-dose TTR knockdown. We propose glycans sterically block IgM docking without preventing ApoE engagement. Liver still dominated uptake. Endosomal escape was unchanged. A limitation is glycan batch variability in manufacturing. These data separate stealth durability from extrahepatic tropism as independent design goals.

title: In vivo CRISPR base editing of hematopoietic niches via bone-marrow tropic LNPs
abstract: Bone-marrow tropic helper lipids increased CD34-enriched editing 2.4-fold versus MC3 LNPs after IV dosing in humanized mice. We hypothesized that phosphatidylserine display mimics apoptotic vesicles and enhances marrow macrophage bridging toward HSCs. Editing in true long-term HSCs remained below 8%. Endosomal escape in resting HSCs was less than 2%. The exact bridging mechanism remains poorly understood. Scaling lipid supply and avoiding off-target marrow inflammation are unresolved translational barriers.

title: N1-methylpseudouridine positional isomers differentially affect TLR sensing and LNP potency
abstract: Systematic placement of m1Ψ versus Ψ across codon positions revealed innate sensing is not a simple function of modification fraction. We propose ribosome dwell time modulates endosomal TLR exposure via altered unpackaging kinetics. Experimental results showed certain isomer patterns cut IFN reporter activity 2-fold at matched protein output. However, the mechanistic link from codon-resolved modification to LNP unpackaging remains speculative. Extrahepatic expression patterns were unchanged. This work highlights a chemistry–delivery co-design gap rarely tested in formulation screens.

title: Hybrid DNA–RNA nanotubes as endosomal rupture nucleation scaffolds
abstract: DNA–RNA hybrid nanotubes were co-assembled with ionizable lipids to nucleate endosomal membrane pores. We hypothesized geometric strain at tube ends lowers the energy barrier for bilayer rupture. In HeLa cells, cytosolic delivery improved 2.8-fold versus lipid-only LNPs at matched dose. Toxicity increased at high tube fractions. In vivo liver expression improved only 1.3-fold, suggesting serum corona dampens nucleation. Direct cryo-ET of tube–endosome contacts in primary cells is still missing. The theory that rigid nucleic acid geometry can replace specialized ionizable lipids remains untested in mammals.

title: Comparative benchmark of bifunctional ncRNA claims against single-payload LNP baselines
abstract: We re-implemented twelve published bifunctional ncRNA–mRNA co-delivery claims under a common LNP baseline. Only three claims reproduced within 20% of reported effect sizes. Failures clustered around unmeasured endosomal escape competition and unreported mass ratios. We propose that field-wide theory outpaced controlled experiments on payload interference. Results show a reproducibility gap specific to hybrid nucleic acid designs. Standardized escape reporters and ratio-reporting checklists are needed before high-impact therapeutic claims can be trusted.

title: Ionizable cationic branched peptides complexed with gRNA for non-liver base editing
abstract: Branched ionizable peptides formed nanocomplexes with adenine base editor gRNA and mRNA, achieving 12% editing in lung endothelium after IV dosing with SORT helpers. We hypothesized peptide branching improves endosomal buffering versus linear peptides. Editing remained far below hepatic levels. Immunogenicity of peptide carriers rose on dose 2. A key limitation is poorly characterized peptide–RNA structure inside endosomes. These data extend hybrid delivery beyond classic four-component LNPs but do not yet solve extrahepatic potency.

title: Single-molecule fluorescence reveals asynchronous cytosolic arrival of co-encapsulated mRNA and ncRNA
abstract: Using orthogonal fluorogenic aptamers, we tracked cytosolic arrival of mRNA and ncRNA co-encapsulated in the same LNP. Arrival was asynchronous: mRNA preceded ncRNA by a median of 4 minutes in hepatocytes, reversing in macrophages. We propose that lipid–cargo affinity, not particle entry, sets escape order. Results falsify the common assumption of simultaneous co-delivery to the cytosol. This timing gap is experimentally actionable and has been under-tested in bifunctional therapy design. Mechanism of cargo-selective membrane partitioning remains poorly understood.
